question.text: Capital gain on REIT units (held > 12 months):

explanation.text: The Logic: Listed REIT units held for more than 12 months qualify as long-term capital assets, and post the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 changes effective July 23, 2024, LTCG on such listed business-trust units is taxed at 12.5% with an aggregate exemption of Rs. 1.25 lakh per financial year (combined with similar listed-equity gains). The Trap: Treating the gain as fully exempt, only the dividend as taxable, or always classifying it as short-term contradicts the listed-unit long-term framework that applies once the 12-month holding threshold is crossed. Note: The specific LTCG-at-12.5%-over-Rs.-1.25-lakh treatment for listed REIT units is not stated in the cited PMS workbook REIT and taxation pages, which cover equity shares and equity-oriented mutual funds. The framing above reflects general post-Finance-Act-2024 capital-gains rules for listed business-trust units rather than a direct workbook citation.
